conventions.convention: Diagrams for the complexity bounds are nonempty, with m ≥ 1. Arcs are cut at undercrossings; a component with no undercrossings contributes one closed arc, so a = c + q ≤ c + m.

A nonzero integer z has signed-magnitude length 1 + ceil(log₂(|z| + 1)); zero has length one. Polynomial coefficient-bit size is the maximum nonzero coefficient length, with value zero for the zero polynomial.
Field operations and equality tests have unit operation cost; this does not give constant bit cost as p varies. Arbitrary literal-code parsing is excluded from typed-diagram operation counts.
The bracket bit-time bound uses the explicitly specified indexed endpoint-pairing input, dense signed binary coefficient arrays, and a fixed finite number of binary work tapes.
The move search takes valid normalized oriented one-component codes, preserves outer-face data under code relabeling, and has no negative-output branch; empty frontiers continue as empty layers.

Countable Choice is assumed for the ambient-isotopy interpretation and smooth code-uniqueness suppliers; the finite state counts, elimination, local coloring bijections, and crossing-distance calculation are choice-free.

load_bearing.statement: Defines crossing and component counts, undercrossing arcs, literal code length, signed-magnitude coefficient-bit size, exact outputs, and field-operation counting.

For a nonempty regular link diagram with c crossings and m components, bracket exponents satisfy |j| ≤ 3c + 2m − 2 and coefficient-bit size is at most m + 2c + 1. The specified indexed exact implementation takes O(2^c(c + m + 1)^4) elementary bit steps.

For an odd prime p, planar isotopy and each oriented R1, R2, or R3 move give an explicit bijection of Fox p-colorings, preserving their number along every finite move sequence without a choice principle.
On a valid normalized oriented one-component code with c crossings, enumerate candidates through crossing bound c + 2 and retain those certified by code relabeling or one oriented R1, R2, or R3 move.

Assuming Countable Choice, breadth-first Reidemeister search returns a finite move witness for ambient-isotopic represented oriented knots. It has no negative-output branch, and failure through a fixed finite depth is not an inequivalence certificate.

concerns.concern: The finite comparison rules say to 'enumerate all finite choices of local edge intervals and crossing subrecords' and 'test that the codes agree outside the chosen disk boundary'. They do not specify finite representatives for interval endpoints or the combinatorial test that the selected boundary bounds an admissible move disk with no additional diagram inside. The intended finite plane-map test is reconstructible, but it is an unstated subprocedure on which termination and completeness in theorem steps 1.1 and 2.1 depend, including the crossingless-circle case.

Step 4 canonicalizes a returned neighbor E but stores only (C, μ), where μ certifies the move to the original representative E. Path reconstruction then uses canonical representatives. The finite relabeling carrying E to its canonical representative should be retained or explicitly incorporated into the certificate interpretation so the returned path has checkable certificates between its displayed representatives.
